status_effects.explanation: Her offhand, teasing tone about their falling-out is experienced by the narrator as callous and horrifying in this moment, a locally negative coloring tempered by his jealousy.

By setting the terms of the exchange and being echoed by Gilberte, the narrator retains conversational initiative and control over the relationship's framing, even as this control rests on a self-constructed fiction.

ambiguities: Gilberte's characterization is genuinely mixed across the passage: sharply cold in the 'continuons à lutter' recollection, but later described as writing letters of real tenderness and delicacy; only the earlier, sharper moment was scored to avoid manufacturing a balancing effect out of material that otherwise reads as essayistic reflection.

appraisal_events.evidence: L'antipathie actuelle de Gilberte pour moi me sembla comme un châtiment... Les mots de Gilberte : « Si vous voulez, continuons à lutter » me firent horreur.
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator reacts with horror to Gilberte's blithe, game-like framing of their broken relationship, casting her as callously indifferent to his suffering, though the judgment is filtered through his jealousy and an imagined rival.

appraisal_events.evidence: un correspondant... est trop heureux de sentir par là qu'il possède – et de garder – la maîtrise et l'initiative des opérations... chaque fois que j'écrivais à Gilberte... elle ne manqua pas de répondre : « La vie a pu nous séparer, elle ne pourra nous faire oublier les bonnes heures... »
appraisal_events.explanation: By engineering an ambiguous rift in his letters, the narrator keeps rhetorical initiative in the correspondence and Gilberte's replies come to mirror his own phrasing, though he admits this leaves him believing in a fiction of his own making.
